projects.title: A place to gather.
projects.name: GMAHK Galilea
projects.summary: Worship resources, community information, and presentation tools in one considered place.
projects.challenge: A community website needs to serve someone finding a service time and someone presenting a hymn on a large screen. Those are very different reading conditions.
projects.approach: Keep the public interface lightweight. Separate the reader, schedule, appearance controls, and presentation behaviors into focused modules.
projects.implementation: A Vercel API layer connects the browser to Google Apps Script. Sheets provide editable content. Service-worker caching, reader preferences, and fullscreen controls support the worship experience.
projects.outcome: The repository contains a public portal, Bible and hymnal readers, Sabbath presentations, theme controls, and operational verification scripts. Performance gains are not quantified here.
projects.tradeoff: Cached public content needs explicit invalidation. Apps Script changes have their own release cycle, separate from a frontend deployment.

projects.title: Files, with a place.
projects.name: Galilea Digital Archive
projects.summary: A cloud-connected archive that makes recurring records easier to find and manage.
projects.challenge: Recurring documents and media need predictable organization without giving every visitor administrative access to cloud storage.
projects.approach: Organize records by category and time, then put authentication and folder boundaries between the interface and Google Drive.
projects.implementation: Next.js route handlers coordinate Drive API operations. Firebase verifies identity and stores records. Resumable upload helpers, a queue, cache utilities, and download routes separate the main responsibilities.
projects.outcome: Source inspection confirms archive browsing, upload handling, media endpoints, and administrative routes. The exhibit below is a local simulation using fictional records.
projects.tradeoff: OAuth credentials and Drive quotas remain external dependencies. A successful interface render alone does not prove every production upload path works.

projects.title: Less fragmentation.
projects.name: Majelis Galilea
projects.summary: Meetings, decisions, budgets, and documents connected through a shared administrative system.
projects.challenge: Administrative work crosses many boundaries: a meeting produces a decision, a decision produces an assignment, and an assignment may affect a budget or document.
projects.approach: Connect the workflow around shared records and explicit permissions, with a clearer interface for each responsibility.
projects.implementation: A browser administration shell calls a Vercel proxy and Apps Script business logic. Sheets hold related records; the backend contains role checks and document-generation workflows.
projects.outcome: The source includes meeting and governance workflows, finance, membership, assets, and official correspondence. No confidential administrative records are reproduced.
projects.tradeoff: Sheets is familiar to operators, but relational integrity, concurrent edits, and authorization require deliberate application logic.

projects.title: The pace of a story.
projects.name: Naomi Rouli
projects.summary: An editorial study in typography, quiet movement, and the space between chapters.
projects.challenge: A personal story needs pacing and emotional clarity without turning every screen into another effect.
projects.approach: Structure the experience into nine scenes. Let typography, composition, and chapter changes carry the narrative.
projects.implementation: Vanilla JavaScript uses IntersectionObserver for chapter navigation and pointer capture for a horizontal photo rail. CSS custom properties maintain the editorial system.
projects.outcome: The public repository supports the interaction techniques described here. This exhibit uses an original typographic illustration; private photographs and personal letters are not reused.
projects.tradeoff: The interface is intentionally bespoke. Reusing its technical patterns is more appropriate than republishing its personal content.

projects.title: Learning restraint.
projects.name: Zvenians Web Exploration
projects.summary: An independent study of product composition, responsive rhythm, and disciplined typography.
projects.challenge: Understand how a consistent visual system can support different product stories across a static website.
projects.approach: Work with type scale, whitespace, full-width compositions, and responsive layouts before adding interaction.
projects.implementation: Semantic HTML, CSS layout primitives, and lightweight JavaScript. GitHub Pages hosts the static output.
projects.outcome: An independent educational design exploration, not a commercial engagement or an official Apple website.
projects.tradeoff: Promotional imagery in the original project is not republished here. This case study focuses on layout techniques.

projects.title: Every system starts somewhere.
projects.name: Galilea Origins
projects.summary: A historical marker connecting an early idea to the later, dedicated platforms.
projects.challenge: The early namespace represents the beginning of a broader church web initiative.
projects.approach: Keep the historical context visible without counting it as another completed application.
projects.implementation: At the audited revision, this repository contains a README only. The active implementations live in the three dedicated Galilea repositories.
projects.outcome: Useful as a timeline marker, not evidence of a functioning prototype.
projects.tradeoff: No executable application was found in this repository.
